en.name: Regional Museum of Natural History Mysore
en.text: A museum opened in 1995 in Mysore showcasing the flora and fauna of South India.

en.name: Mysore Palace
en.text: The magnificent residence of the Wodeyar dynasty, famous for its golden throne and Indo-Saracenic style.

en.name: University Folklore Museum
en.text: A museum of the University of Mysore housing a vast collection of South Indian folk art.

en.name: St. Philomena's Church
en.text: A Neo-Gothic cathedral in Mysore modeled after the Cologne Cathedral in Germany.

en.name: Sri Chamundeshwari Temple
en.text: This 12th-century Dravidian-style temple sits atop Chamundi Hill and is accessible via a climb of over 1,000 steps.

en.name: Sri Chamarajendra Zoological Garden
en.text: Founded in 1892, this zoo is one of India's oldest and houses rare species across its expansive grounds.

en.name: Payana Car Museum
en.text: Housed in a unique tyre-shaped building, this museum displays over 70 vintage and classic vehicles.

en.name: Indira Gandhi Rashtriya Manav Sangrahalaya
en.text: Located in the historic Wellington Lodge, this museum is dedicated to preserving India's diverse tribal cultures.

en.name: House of R. K. Narayan
en.text: The former residence of the author of 'Malgudi Days' displays personal artifacts and literary works of the writer.

en.name: Kaveri Kala Kuteera
en.text: This art center near the Oriental Research Institute showcases local handicrafts and traditional artifacts.

en.name: Sandalwood Oil Factory
en.text: Established in 1916, this factory is famous for producing authentic Mysore sandalwood oil and the renowned soap.

en.name: Melody World Wax Museum
en.text: This wax museum houses over 300 musical instruments and life-size wax statues of famous musicians.

en.name: Sand museum
en.text: India’s first sand sculpture museum displays over 150 detailed artworks crafted entirely from sand.

en.name: Jaganmohan Palace and Art Gallery
en.text: Built in traditional Hindu style, this palace houses a significant art gallery featuring Raja Ravi Varma's original paintings.

en.name: Mysuru Rail Museum
en.text: India's second railway museum displays historic locomotives and the Maharaja’s ornate saloon carriage.

en.name: Vishwam Museum
en.text: Located within the SGS Ashrama, this museum features an eclectic collection of minerals, gemstones, and traditional musical instruments.

en.name: Narasimharaja Wodeyar
en.text: This monument near Hardinge Circle commemorates the Mysore prince Kanteerava Narasimharaja Wodeyar.

en.name: Krishnaraja Wodeyar
en.text: This central statue at KR Circle honors Nalwadi Krishnaraja Wodeyar, a significant reformer and ruler of Mysore.

en.name: Amphitheatre
en.text: This amphitheatre by the palace is used for ceremonies and cultural performances during the famous Dasara festival.

en.name: Naada Mantapa
en.text: This magnificent concert hall at SGS Ashrama seats 4,000 and is renowned for its exceptional acoustics.

en.name: Naadabrhma Sangeetha Sabha
en.text: This historic music hall is a key center for classical Carnatic music and cultural events in Mysore.

en.name: Mysore Medical College Auditorium
en.text: This medical college auditorium serves as a venue for academic conferences and student ceremonies.

en.name: Auditorium
en.text: This central assembly hall on the university campus hosts academic lectures and official celebrations.

en.name: Humanities Auditorium
en.text: Located in the university's humanities block, this auditorium serves as a forum for debates and cultural evenings.

en.name: Open Air Theatre
en.text: This spacious 10,000-seat open-air theatre has previously hosted the Indian Science Congress.

en.name: Gandhi Auditorium
en.text: This building dedicated to Mahatma Gandhi's memory features sculptures depicting the historic Salt March.

en.name: Kala Mandira
en.text: This major cultural center in Mysore serves as a stage for theatre plays, dance recitals, and art exhibitions.

en.name: Maharaja College Centenary Hall
en.text: Built in 1951 for the Maharaja’s College centenary, this hall is a landmark of campus architecture.

en.name: Veena Sheshanna Bhavana
en.text: Named after the royal musician Veena Sheshanna, this building is a venue for classical concerts and cultural gatherings.

en.name: Raghavendra Swamy Temple
en.text: This temple dedicated to the saint Raghavendra Swamy is a significant religious site for followers of the Madhva tradition.

en.name: Sri Lakshminarasimha Temple
en.text: This shrine is dedicated to the lion incarnation of Vishnu and features detailed sculptures of Hindu deities.

en.name: Chamundi Hill
en.text: This 1,063m high hill is home to a massive 5-meter Nandi statue carved from a single piece of rock.

en.name: Wesley Cathedral
en.text: Founded in 1871, this Methodist church was built on land gifted by the Maharaja of Mysore.

en.name: Eidgah Maidan
en.text: This spacious open ground serves as a central location for the Muslim community's major Eid prayers.

en.name: Tattva Jnana Mandira
en.text: This center is dedicated to the study of Indian philosophy and houses a library of spiritual texts.

en.name: Church
en.text: This colonial-era Christian place of worship is known for its simple architecture and quiet courtyard.

en.name: Ganesha Temple
en.text: A local temple dedicated to the elephant-headed god Ganesha, frequently visited by devotees before new undertakings.

descriptionAdvanced.de: Der Mysore-Palast, auch Amba Vilas Palast genannt, ist die offizielle Residenz der Wodeyar-Dynastie in Mysuru. Das heutige Gebäude wurde zwischen 1897 und 1912 errichtet, nachdem der ursprüngliche Holzpalast während einer Hochzeitsfeier abgebrannt war. Der britische Architekt Henry Irwin entwarf das Bauwerk im indo-sarazenischen Stil, einer eklektischen Mischung aus hinduistischen, muslimischen, rajputischen und gotischen Elementen. Der Palast ist berühmt für seine prächtigen Innenräume, darunter die öffentliche Audienzhalle (Durbar Hall) mit ihren verzierten Säulen und die private Audienzhalle mit Buntglasfenstern. Jedes Jahr während des Dasara-Festes wird die Fassade des Palastes von fast 100.000 Glühbirnen beleuchtet, was ihn zu einer der meistbesuchten Sehenswürdigkeiten Indiens nach dem Taj Mahal macht. Das Gebäude beherbergt zudem eine umfangreiche Sammlung von königlichen Artefakten und Gemälden.
descriptionAdvanced.hu: A Mysore-palota, más néven Amba Vilas palota, a Wodeyar-dinasztia hivatalos rezidenciája Mysuru városában. A mai épületet 1897 és 1912 között emelték, miután az eredeti fapalota egy esküvői ünnepség során leégett. Henry Irwin brit építész tervezte az építményt indo-szaracén stílusban, amely a hindu, muszlim, radzsput és gótikus elemek eklektikus keveréke. A palota híres pazar belső tereiről, köztük a díszes oszlopokkal ellátott nyilvános audienciateremről (Durbar Hall) és a színes üvegablakokkal díszített magánteremről. Minden évben a Dasara-fesztivál idején a palota homlokzatát közel 100 000 izzó világítja meg, így a Taj Mahal után India egyik leglátogatottabb nevezetessége. Az épület emellett királyi műtárgyak és festmények kiterjedt gyűjteményének ad otthont.
descriptionAdvanced.ro: Palatul Mysore, cunoscut și sub numele de Palatul Amba Vilas, este reședința oficială a dinastiei Wodeyar din Mysuru. Actuala clădire a fost construită între 1897 și 1912, după ce palatul original din lemn a ars în timpul unei ceremonii de nuntă. Arhitectul britanic Henry Irwin a proiectat structura în stil indo-sarazin, o amestecătură eclectică de elemente hinduise, musulmane, rajput și gotice. Palatul este renumit pentru interioarele sale opulente, inclusiv sala de audiențe publice (Durbar Hall) cu coloane decorate și sala privată cu vitralii. În fiecare an, în timpul festivalului Dasara, fațada palatului este iluminată de aproape 100.000 de becuri, făcându-l una dintre cele mai vizitate atracții din India după Taj Mahal. Clădirea găzduiește, de asemenea, o colecție vastă de artefacte regale și picturi.
descriptionAdvanced.en: The Mysore Palace, also known as Amba Vilas Palace, is the official residence of the Wodeyar dynasty in Mysuru. The current structure was constructed between 1897 and 1912 after the original wooden palace was destroyed by fire during a wedding celebration. British architect Henry Irwin designed the building in the Indo-Saracenic style, which is an eclectic blend of Hindu, Muslim, Rajput, and Gothic architectural elements. The palace is famous for its magnificent interiors, including the public Durbar Hall with its ornate columns and the private audience hall featuring stained-glass ceilings. Every year during the Dasara festival, the palace exterior is illuminated by nearly 100,000 light bulbs, making it one of India's most visited landmarks after the Taj Mahal. The complex also houses a vast collection of royal artifacts, weapons, and historical paintings.
descriptionAdvanced.es: El Palacio de Mysore es un lugar de interés destacado en el estado indio de Karnataka. Es un palacio histórico y residencia real en Mysore. Sirve como residencia oficial de la dinastía Wadiyar y sede del Reino de Mysore. Desde una perspectiva regional, el lugar representa la diversidad y complejidad de esta parte de la India. Se centra en varios aspectos: es una de las atracciones turísticas más famosas de la India. Su arquitectura es una mezcla de estilos hindú, mogol, rajput y gótico. Por ello, el Palacio de Mysore es uno de los ejemplos más característicos de Karnataka y de la India en general. Cultura K7 — Monumentos y Patrimonio de la Humanidad de la India.

Il est la résidence officielle de la dynastie Wadiyar et le siège du royaume de Mysore. D'un point de vue régional, le site illustre la diversité et la complexité de cette partie de l'Inde. es: El Palacio de Mysore se encuentra en el estado de Karnataka y es un lugar de interés muy conocido.
La región atrae anualmente a numerosos visitantes de toda la India y del extranjero.
La cultura y el idioma locales están estrechamente vinculados a la identidad de Karnataka.
El Palacio de Mysore figura como punto de referencia en muchos mapas de la India.
